summary: A security gateway that protects legacy systems that cannot easily be updated, by isolating them on a private network and placing a reverse proxy in front of them that adds authentication, MFA, encryption, access control, and audit logging without modifying the legacy application.

requirements.title: Legacy demo application
requirements.story: As a system owner, I want a simple legacy web application to stand in for a real outdated system, so that the gateway can be demonstrated against a realistic target.
acceptance: Serves a small records-style web app (list, view, and edit records) over plain HTTP
Has no built-in authentication, encryption, or logging
Runs in its own container on a fixed internal port

requirements.title: Containerized deployment
requirements.story: As an IT administrator, I want the gateway and legacy app deployed as separate containers, so that the whole system can be started consistently with one command.
acceptance: A Docker Compose file starts the gateway, legacy app, and database
`docker compose up` brings up a working system from a fresh clone
Each service runs in its own container

requirements.title: Network isolation of the legacy app
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want the legacy app reachable only through the gateway, so that no one can bypass the security controls.
acceptance: Legacy app is attached only to an internal Docker network with no published ports
Direct requests to the legacy app from the host or outside network fail
The gateway is the only service attached to both the internal and external networks

requirements.title: Reverse proxy request forwarding
requirements.story: As an end user, I want my requests passed through to the legacy app transparently, so that I can use it exactly as before.
acceptance: GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE requests are forwarded with headers, query strings, and bodies intact
Responses (status, headers, body) are returned to the client unchanged except for gateway-added security headers
All legacy app pages and forms work through the gateway

requirements.title: No modifications to the legacy app
requirements.story: As a system owner, I want the gateway to work without any changes to the legacy app's code, so that systems that can't be modified can still be protected.
acceptance: Legacy app source is unchanged between the unprotected and protected demos
All security features are implemented in the gateway

requirements.title: Upstream failure handling
requirements.story: As an end user, I want a clear error page when the legacy app is down, so that I know the problem isn't on my end.
acceptance: Gateway returns a 502/503 page with a friendly message when the legacy app is unreachable
Upstream timeouts are configurable

requirements.title: User account store
requirements.story: As an IT administrator, I want a database of gateway users, so that access can be granted and revoked per person.
acceptance: Stores username, password hash, role, account status, and MFA secret
Disabled accounts cannot log in
A seed script creates an initial admin account

requirements.title: Secure password storage
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want passwords stored with a strong hashing algorithm, so that a database leak doesn't expose user passwords.
acceptance: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt or Argon2 using per-user salts
Plaintext passwords are never stored or logged

requirements.title: Login and session management
requirements.story: As an end user, I want to log in once and stay authenticated, so that I can use the legacy app securely without re-entering credentials on every page.
acceptance: Unauthenticated requests are redirected to the gateway's login page
Successful login creates a session cookie marked HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite
Session IDs are regenerated on login
After login, the user is sent to the page they originally requested

requirements.title: Logout and session expiry
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want sessions to expire after inactivity, so that unattended workstations don't stay logged in.
acceptance: Users can log out, which invalidates the session server-side
Sessions expire after a configurable idle timeout

requirements.title: Brute-force protection
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want repeated failed logins to be throttled, so that attackers can't guess passwords.
acceptance: An account is temporarily locked after a configurable number of failed attempts
Login attempts are rate-limited per IP address
Lockouts are recorded in the audit log

requirements.title: MFA enrollment (TOTP)
requirements.story: As an end user, I want to enroll an authenticator app, so that my account is protected even if my password is stolen.
acceptance: User can enroll by scanning a QR code with an authenticator app
Enrollment is confirmed only after a valid code is entered
MFA secrets are stored securely in the user store

requirements.title: MFA verification at login
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want users to enter a one-time code after their password, so that a stolen password alone isn't enough to get in.
acceptance: Enrolled users must enter a valid TOTP code before a session is created
Invalid or reused codes are rejected
Admins can require MFA for all users

requirements.title: Role-based access control
requirements.story: As an IT administrator, I want to assign roles to users, so that people only get the access their job requires.
acceptance: Supports at least admin and standard user roles
Gateway admin pages are restricted to admins
A user's role is checked on every request

requirements.title: Path-level access rules
requirements.story: As an IT administrator, I want to restrict which parts of the legacy app each role can reach, so that sensitive functions are protected even though the app has no permissions of its own.
acceptance: Rules map roles to allowed URL paths and HTTP methods in a config file
Requests that match no rule are denied by default
Denied requests return 403 and are logged

requirements.title: HTTPS termination
requirements.story: As an end user, I want my connection to the gateway encrypted, so that credentials and data can't be read on the network.
acceptance: Gateway serves all traffic over TLS 1.2 or higher
Plain HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS
Works with a self-signed certificate for local demos

requirements.title: Security response headers
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want the gateway to add modern security headers, so that browsers get protections the legacy app never set.
acceptance: Adds HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and a basic Content-Security-Policy
Headers are added without breaking legacy app pages

requirements.title: Request audit logging
requirements.story: As a compliance officer, I want every request through the gateway recorded, so that access to the legacy system can be audited.
acceptance: Each request logs timestamp, user, source IP, method, path, response status, and allow/deny decision
Logs are stored in the database
Sensitive values (passwords, session tokens) are never logged

requirements.title: Authentication event logging
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want login activity recorded, so that I can investigate suspicious access attempts.
acceptance: Logs successful and failed logins, MFA failures, lockouts, and logouts
Each event includes username, source IP, and timestamp

requirements.title: Tamper-evident log storage
requirements.story: As a compliance officer, I want audit logs protected from modification, so that records can be trusted during an investigation.
acceptance: Log entries are append-only through the application
Each entry includes a hash of the previous entry, forming a verifiable chain
A verification command reports whether any entry was altered

requirements.title: Audit log dashboard
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want to view and filter logs in a web dashboard, so that I can review activity without querying the database.
acceptance: Admin-only page lists log entries, newest first, with pagination
Entries can be filtered by user, date range, path, and allow/deny decision

requirements.title: User management interface
requirements.story: As an IT administrator, I want to manage gateway users from the dashboard, so that I can grant and revoke access quickly.
acceptance: Admins can create, disable, and re-enable users
Admins can assign roles and reset a user's MFA enrollment
All admin actions are logged

requirements.title: Suspicious activity detection
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want unusual behavior flagged automatically, so that potential attacks or misuse are noticed early.
acceptance: Flags repeated failed logins, logins at unusual hours for that user, abnormal request volume, and repeated denied requests
Detection thresholds are configurable
Each flag records the rule triggered and the related log entries

requirements.title: Security alerts on dashboard
requirements.story: As a security administrator, I want flagged events shown prominently in the dashboard, so that I can respond to them quickly.
acceptance: Dashboard shows open alerts with severity and time
Admins can mark alerts as reviewed

requirements.title: Gateway configuration
requirements.story: As an IT administrator, I want gateway settings in a config file and environment variables, so that the gateway can protect different legacy apps without code changes.
acceptance: Upstream URL, ports, timeouts, and session settings are configurable
Secrets (session keys, database credentials) come from environment variables and are never committed

requirements.title: Performance overhead
requirements.story: As an end user, I want the gateway to add minimal delay, so that the legacy app feels as responsive as before.
acceptance: Median added latency is under 100 ms in the demo environment
Latency is measured with a repeatable benchmark documented in the repo

requirements.title: Automated tests
requirements.story: As a developer, I want automated tests for the gateway's security features, so that changes don't silently break protection.
acceptance: Unit tests cover password hashing, sessions, MFA verification, and access rules
An integration test confirms the legacy app cannot be reached directly
Tests run in CI on every pull request

requirements.title: Setup and architecture documentation
requirements.story: As a developer, I want clear setup and architecture docs, so that anyone can run and understand the project.
acceptance: README explains setup, configuration, and running the demo
Architecture diagram shows the request flow and network isolation

requirements.title: Non-HTTP protocol support (e.g., DICOM)
requirements.story: As a hospital IT administrator, I want the gateway to protect devices that use medical protocols like DICOM, so that equipment such as MRI systems can be secured.
acceptance: Out of scope this term; documented as future work

requirements.title: Single sign-on with external identity providers
requirements.story: As an IT administrator, I want users to sign in with the organization's existing identity provider (OIDC/SAML), so that they don't need separate gateway accounts.
acceptance: Out of scope this term; documented as future work
